content_sanskrit: अथ गच्छति कालेऽत्र जराजर्जरितायुषि । तुषारपूर्णशष्पौघसमश्मश्रुभृते मयि
padaccheda: अथ । गच्छति । काले । अत्र । जराजर्जरितायुषि । तुषारपूर्णशष्पौघसमश्मश्रुभृते । मयि
anvaya: अथ अत्र काले गच्छति (सति), तुषार-पूर्ण-शष्प-ओघ-सम-श्मश्रु-भृते जराजर्जरित-आयुषि मयि (सति)
meaning_english: Then, as time passed, my life became worn out by old age, and I bore a beard resembling a heap of young grass covered with frost.

padaccheda: कर्मवातापनुन्नेषु । सरसेषु । अरसेषु । अपि । पतत्सु । वासरौघेषु । शीर्णपर्णगणेषु । इव
anvaya: कर्म-वात-अपनुन्नेषु सरसेषु अरसेषु अपि वासर-ओघेषु शीर्ण-पर्ण-गणेषु इव पतत्सु (सत्सु)
meaning_english: The days, whether pleasant or unpleasant, passed away like falling withered leaves, driven by the winds of past actions.

content_sanskrit: आजाविव शरौघेषु सुखदुःखेष्वनारतम् । कलहेष्वप्यकार्येषु चागच्छत्सु पतत्सु च
padaccheda: आजौ । इव । शरौघेषु । सुखदुःखेषु । अनारतम् । कलहेषु । अपि । अकार्येषु । च । आगच्छत्सु । पतत्सु । च
anvaya: आजौ शर-ओघेषु इव सुख-दुःखेषु अनारतम् कलहेषु अपि अकार्येषु च आगच्छत्सु पतत्सु च (सत्सु)
meaning_english: Joys and sorrows, along with conflicts and improper deeds, continuously arrived and fell upon me like showers of arrows in a battle.

content_sanskrit: विकल्पकल्पनावर्तवर्तिनि द्विजगे जडे । समुद्र इव कल्लोलभरे भ्रमितचेतसि
padaccheda: विकल्पकल्पनावर्तवर्तिनि । द्विजगे । जडे । समुद्रे । इव । कल्लोलभरे । भ्रमितचेतसि
anvaya: विकल्प-कल्पना-आवर्त-वर्तिनि जडे द्विज-गे (तथा) कल्लोल-भरे समुद्रे इव भ्रमित-चेतसि (सति)
meaning_english: My mind wandered like a sea filled with waves, caught in the whirlpools of doubts and imaginations, remaining dull within the body of a low-born man.

content_sanskrit: चलच्चिन्ताचितं चक्रमारूढे भ्रान्त आत्मनि । प्रोह्यमाने तृण इव सावर्तं कालसागरे
padaccheda: चलच्चिन्ताचितम् । चक्रम् । आरूढे । भ्रान्ते । आत्मनि । प्रोह्यमाने । तृणे । इव । सावर्तम् । कालसागरे
anvaya: चलत्-चिन्ता-चितं चक्रम् आरूढे भ्रान्ते आत्मनि (सति), स-आवर्तं काल-सागरे तृणे इव प्रोह्यमाने (सति)
meaning_english: My confused self, mounted on the wheel of restless thoughts, was swept away like a blade of grass in the turbulent ocean of time.

content_sanskrit: विन्ध्योर्वीवनकीटस्य ग्रासैकशरणस्य मे । द्विबाहोर्गर्दभस्यात्र क्षीण इत्थं समागणे
padaccheda: विन्ध्योर्वीवनकीटस्य । ग्रासैकशरणस्य । मे । द्विबाहोः । गर्दभस्य । अत्र । क्षीणे । इत्थम् । समागणे
anvaya: विन्ध्य-उर्वी-वन-कीटस्य ग्रास-एक-शरणस्य द्विबाहोः गर्दभस्य मे अत्र समा-गणे इत्थं क्षीणे (सति)
meaning_english: Living like a worm in the forests of the Vindhya mountains, I was a two-armed donkey whose only refuge was seeking food, as my years thus dwindled away.

content_sanskrit: विस्मृते मम भूपत्वे शवस्येव महाजवे । चाण्डालत्वे स्थिरीभूते पक्षच्छिन्न इवाचले
padaccheda: विस्मृते । मम । भूपत्वे । शवस्य । इव । महाजवे । चाण्डालत्वे । स्थिरीभूते । पक्षच्छिन्ने । इव । अचले
anvaya: मम भूपत्वे विस्मृते (सति), महा-जवे शवस्य इव (अथवा) पक्ष-च्छिन्ने अचले इव चाण्डालत्वे स्थिरीभूते (सति)
meaning_english: My former kingship was forgotten; I was firmly established in the state of an outcaste, like a corpse lost in speed or a mountain whose wings have been clipped.

content_sanskrit: संसारमिव कल्पान्तो दावाग्निरिव काननम् । सागरोर्मिस्तटमिव शुष्कवृक्षमिवाशनिः
padaccheda: संसारम् । इव । कल्पान्तः । दावाग्निः । इव । काननम् । सागरोर्मिः । तटम् । इव । शुष्कवृक्षम् । इव । अशनिः
anvaya: कल्प-अन्तः संसारम् इव, दावाग्निः काननम् इव, सागर-ऊर्मिः तटम् इव, अशनिः शुष्क-वृक्षम् इव
meaning_english: Just as the end of an aeon destroys the world, a forest fire consumes the woods, a wave hits the shore, or a thunderbolt strikes a dry tree,

content_sanskrit: अकाण्डे मरणोड्डीनं चण्डचण्डालमण्डलम् । निरन्नतृणपत्राम्बु विन्ध्यकच्छं तदाययौ
padaccheda: अकाण्डे । मरणोड्डीनम् । चण्डचाण्डालमण्डलम् । निरन्नतृणपत्राम्बु । विन्ध्यकच्छम् । तदा । आययौ
anvaya: तदा अकाण्डे मरण-उड्रीनम् चण्ड-चाण्डाल-मण्डलम् नि-अन्न-तृण-पत्र-अम्बु विन्ध्य-कच्छम् आययौ
meaning_english: Then, a terrible famine suddenly struck the Vindhya region, devoid of grain, grass, leaves, or water, driving the fierce outcaste tribe toward death.

content_sanskrit: न वर्षति घनव्राते दृष्टनष्टे क्वचित्स्थिते । पूतांगारकणोन्मिश्रगतौ वहति मारुते
padaccheda: न । वर्षति । घनव्राते । दृष्टनष्टे । क्वचित् । स्थिते । पूतांगारकणोन्मिश्रगतौ । वहति । मारुते
anvaya: घन-व्राते न वर्षति (सति), क्वचित् स्थिते (अथवा) दृष्ट-नष्टे (सति), पूत-अङ्गार-कण-उन्मिश्र-गतौ मारुते वहति (सति)
meaning_english: The clouds did not rain but vanished as soon as they were seen, while the wind blew with the heat of purified charcoal embers.

content_sanskrit: शीर्णमर्मरपर्णासु दावाग्निवलितासु च । वनस्थलीषु शून्यासु चिरप्रव्रजितास्विव
padaccheda: शीर्णमर्मरपर्णासु । दावाग्निवलितासु । च । वनस्थलीषु । शून्यासु । चिरप्रव्रजितासु । इव
anvaya: शीर्ण-मर्मर-पर्णासु (च) दावाग्नि-वलितासु चिर-प्रव्रजितासु इव शून्यासु वन-स्थलीषु (तत् अभवत्)
meaning_english: In the desolate forest regions, filled with withered and rustling leaves and encircled by forest fires, there was a void resembling those who have long since wandered away as ascetics.

padaccheda: अकाण्डम् । अभवत् । भीमम् । उद्दामदवपावकम् । शोषिताशेषगहनम् । भस्मशेषतृणोलपम्
meaning_english: Suddenly, a terrifying and unrestrained forest fire broke out, drying up the entire dense thicket and leaving behind only ashes of the grass and reeds.
The entire region of the forest fire became a place where all bodies were grey with dust, every human was starving, and there was a total lack of food, grass, and water.
Groups of buffaloes were sinking into the shimmering waters of the desert mirage, while the forest sky was filled with an overflow of spray-clouds raised by the wind.
Crowds of men were intensely eager just to hear the sound of water, while every human being was suffering and wasting away from the intense heat of the sun.
The starving creatures were desperately rising to seize and devour leaves, their teeth gnashing and rolling in an attempt to chew even their own limbs.
Mistaking them for meat, they swallowed heaps of fierce sparks from khadira wood, and swallowed forest stones thinking they were small cakes or frogs.
Groups of mothers, sons, and fathers clung to one another in desperation, while excellent sārikā birds, swallowed by vultures, cried out from within their bellies.
The ground was drenched with blood from the severed limbs of one another, and intoxicated, hungry elephants were intent on devouring lions.
The scene was terrifying with lions wandering individually to swallow the caves, and it bore the chaos created by powerful men intent on devouring each other.
That region was filled with winds carrying mature embers flying from leafless trees, and its mineral-rich slopes resembled land licked by cats eager to drink blood.
The forest winds whirled with the impact of dense masses of flames, while the entire jungle turned tawny due to heaps of roaring fires everywhere.
Thick bushes of smoke rose from burnt pythons and elephants, while the sky was enveloped by clouds of dusk-like flames whirled by the wind.
The region echoed with violent noises, its atmosphere pillar-less due to flying ashes, and filled with the cries of miserable children and wailing women.
Terrified crowds of men bit into large corpses with their teeth, even devouring their own blood-stained fingers in their haste driven by the smell of flesh.
Drunken by the dense hue of smoke mistaken for blue leafy creepers, wandering vultures swallowed fierce firebrands flying in the sky, mistaking them for meat.
The place was chaotic with people fleeing with mangled limbs, their hearts and bellies bursting from the crackling sounds of the blazing fire.
The forest fire leaped terrifyingly with the howling of wind in hollows, while trees rained embers due to the hissing of frightened pythons.

content_sanskrit: सदकाण्डस्फुटद्देशं प्राप्य तच्छुष्ककोटरम् । द्वादशार्काग्निदग्धस्य जगतोऽनुकृतिं ययौ
padaccheda: स-अकाण्ड-स्फुटत्-देशम् । प्राप्य । तत् । शुष्क-कोटरम् । द्वादश-अर्क-अग्नि-दग्धस्य । जगतः । अनुकृतिम् । ययौ
anvaya: सः (देशः) तद् शुष्क-कोटरम् प्राप्य स-अकाण्ड-स्फुटत्-देशम् (सन्) द्वादश-अर्क-अग्नि-दग्धस्य जगतः अनुकृतिम् ययौ ।
meaning_english: Reaching those dry hollows and bursting apart unexpectedly, that region took on the appearance of a world being consumed by the fires of the twelve suns.
With people driven away by the spreading winds from clusters of trees massed with blazing fire, the land resembled the pleasure-house of Agni, Sūrya, and Yama.
